papers.title: Can Facebook Ads Prevent Malaria? Two Field Experiments in India
papers.authors: Dante Donati, Nandan Rao, Victor Orozco-Olvera, Ana Maria Muñoz Boudet
papers.abstract: Two field experiments evaluate a nationwide Facebook malaria prevention campaign in India, finding effects concentrated in urban, more advantaged populations.

papers.title: From Data to Decisions: Marketing Analytics, Mental Performance, and Firm Growth in an Emerging Market
papers.authors: Stephen J. Anderson, Pradeep K. Chintagunta, Rupali Kaul, Naufel J. Vilcassim
papers.abstract: Using a field experiment with 550 Rwandan firms, we show marketing analytics causally enhances entrepreneurs’ cognition and raises firm sales and profits.

papers.title: Music Marketing with Generative AI
papers.abstract: The multibillion-dollar music industry faces severe content creation bottlenecks, making multimedia marketing assets prohibitively costly for smaller artists. This practice paper introduces a Marketing Asset Generation Engine (MAGE) that can produce over 700 million video ad variations reflecting each artist’s visual identity using only a music track’s audio and album cover as inputs. Collaborating with one of the world’s largest music labels, we conduct four preregistered field studies with over 11 million impressions across 75 campaigns for 33 music tracks on TikTok and Meta to validate MAGE. First, pooled across studies, MAGE-generated ads significantly outperform human-designed ads on TikTok with on average 26% higher click-through rates and 10% higher engagement, while we do not detect statistically significant performance differences on Meta, all at 98% lower production cost. Second, neither marketing professionals nor laypeople can reliably identify winning ads such that random sampling of MAGE’s outputs performs as well as human-curated selections. In contrast, an AI-in-the-loop system trained on past performance data can predict pre-launch which MAGE-generated ads will perform best for specific audience segments. These findings demonstrate that generative AI democratizes music marketing by making effective, on-brand video ads accessible at scale.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Correcting omitted-variable bias without instruments: An ICA-based alternative to Gaussian copula methods
papers.abstract: This paper proposes an instrument-free correction for omitted-variable bias and overcomes a key limitation of Gaussian copula control function (GCCF) approaches. Omitted-variable bias is the most common source of endogeneity in marketing, and many articles apply GCCF to address it. Yet GCCF require a nonlinear regressor-error relation, whereas textbooks assume linear, additive relationships between regressors and omitted variables. The authors prove that GCCF is biased in classical omitted-variable settings. Extant articles that address omitted-variables with GCCF also show language cues implicitly assuming linear relationships, which invalidate the use of GCCF. The proposed endogeneity correction is tailored to this prominent case, utilizing independent component analysis (ICA). It assumes a latent normally distributed component that additively influences both the endogenous regressor and the error. This can be interpreted as the sum of omitted variables, which, according to the Central Limit Theorem, add up to a normal distribution. Through ICA, this component is identified and extracted from the endogenous regressor, rendering the regression model free of endogeneity and enabling causal inference. The paper proves that the model is point-identified despite endogeneity due to omitted variables, that the proposed estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal, and that Jackknife resampling yields valid standard errors.

papers.title: EXPRESS: The Role of Digital Ad Clutter in Ad Viewership and Memory
papers.authors: Sean Melessa, Poet Larsen, Paul Hoban
papers.abstract:
Advertisers face an increasingly cluttered digital ecosystem where customer attention matters. Despite this, the extent to which digital advertising clutter influences ad viewership remains unclear. This paper presents three separate eye-tracking experiments (subjects:
                    N
                    = 99,
                    N
                    = 250, and
                    N
                    = 575) using over a dozen custom-built web pages to better understand how digital ad clutter affects consumers’ viewing of digital ads. Across experiments, we show that increased clutter led consumers to allocate more attention to the overall advertising space and adjust how they distribute viewership across ad positions. A complementary survey revealed that clutter also reduced ad memory and recall for individual ads. We discuss the implications for advertisers and publishers regarding ad pricing and placement in crowded digital environments.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Why are products so similar despite diverse consumer needs? The interplay between advertising and horizontal product differentiation
papers.authors: Amit Pazgal, David Soberman, Raphael Thomadsen
papers.abstract: Firms are often less differentiated than standard price-competition models predict. We explain this gap by showing how firms can use informative or reminder advertising to soften competition. When firms choose locations, advertising, and prices endogenously, they may choose to soften price competition through limited advertising rather than greater product differentiation, allowing them to locate closer together while limiting price competition. This outcome of low advertising and central collocation is especially likely when advertising costs are high. We also observe that partially-differentiated equilibria, with one firm locating centrally and the other at an edge, and full differentiation, can each emerge under certain conditions. Thus, firms endogenously choose a mix of advertising and product differentiation to moderate price competition. Further, the shape of travel costs influences the equilibrium outcome. If the disutility from distance is highly convex, such as occurs when consumer preferences exhibit satisficing, central collocation becomes the unique equilibrium when more consumers are concentrated at the edge locations. However, when the disutility from distance is linear, having more customers located towards the edge locations makes collocation less likely. Overall, the interaction of advertising costs, consumer preferences, and location choices help explain why firms often forgo product differentiation.

papers.title: EXPRESS: Expanding Markets or Capturing Share? The Competitive Effects of Subscriptions on Spending in Restaurant Delivery
papers.authors: Daniel M. McCarthy, Shin Oblander, Young-Hoon Park, Yeohong Yoon
papers.abstract: Subscription programs are increasingly central to platform strategy, but their effects on competitors and category demand remain unclear. The authors study restaurant delivery subscriptions using individual-level transaction data on Postmates Unlimited, the first widely available U.S. subscription program in the category, and DoorDash's later DashPass program. Using a matched, staggered difference-in-differences design, they find that signing up for Postmates Unlimited is associated with a 90.4% increase in spending at the focal firm, with no significant average change in competing-firm spending and no offsetting decline in adjacent food categories, consistent with category expansion. Competitive effects depend on customers' prior platform usage. For “singlehomers” (who only used Postmates prior to subscribing), subscribing is associated with increased spending at both the focal firm and competing platforms, even after cancellation. For “multihomers” (who had also previously used competing platforms), the focal-firm effect is larger, and competing-firm spending falls while customers remain subscribed; after cancellation, the focal-firm lift persists, but the decrease in competitor spending does not. DashPass results are broadly similar, but customers with prior Postmates subscription experience show little increase in category spending. Together, these findings suggest subscriptions can both expand markets and capture share, depending on prior platform usage and subscription experience.
